proposals.before: On imperial summons he entered the Grand Master of Ceremonies' school, continued under the erudite Bai Qi, a classmate, and took the Analects and Mourning Dress from Xia housheng.
proposals.after: On imperial summons he entered the Grand Master of Ceremonies' school, continued under the erudite Bai Qi, a classmate, and took the Analects and Mourning Dress from Xiahou Sheng.
proposals.reason: Chinese 夏侯勝 is the name Xiahou Sheng; idiomatic incorrectly splits/fuses it as 'Xia housheng'.

proposals.before: By order he went to the Grand Master of Ceremonies to receive instruction, then studied again under his fellow student the erudite Bai Qi, and also questioned Xia housheng on the Analects and on Mourning Dress.
proposals.after: By order he went to the Grand Master of Ceremonies to receive instruction, then studied again under his fellow student the erudite Bai Qi, and also questioned Xiahou Sheng on the Analects and on Mourning Dress.
proposals.reason: Literal likewise misrenders 夏侯勝 as 'Xia housheng' instead of Xiahou Sheng.

proposals.before: Earlier, when Huhanye Chanyu of the Xiongnu came to court, an edict ordered the dukes and ministers to discuss the proper ritual. Chancellor Bing Ba and Imperial Counselor Yu Dingguo proposed, "In the institutions of the sage kings, virtue is extended and ritual performed first in the capital, then among the central states; first among the central states, then among the Yi and Di peoples.
proposals.after: Earlier, when Huhanye Chanyu of the Xiongnu came to court, an edict ordered the dukes and ministers to discuss the proper ritual. Chancellor Huang Ba and Imperial Counselor Yu Dingguo proposed, "In the institutions of the sage kings, virtue is extended and ritual performed first in the capital, then among the central states; first among the central states, then among the Yi and Di peoples.
proposals.reason: 丞相霸 is Huang Ba (黃霸) from the preceding narrative, not Bing Ba.

proposals.before: Hong Gong and Shi Xian had long run the machinery of state, knew every clause of the code, and moved in lockstep with General Wang Gao, stonewalling Wangzhi with citations of old precedent.
proposals.after: Hong Gong and Shi Xian had long run the machinery of state, knew every clause of the code, and moved in lockstep with General Shi Gao, stonewalling Wangzhi with citations of old precedent.
proposals.reason: 車騎將軍高 is Shi Gao (史高), already named earlier; 'Wang Gao' invents the wrong surname.

proposals.before: Palace secretariat directors Hong Gong and Shi Xian long controlled the levers of government, were expert in written law, and also worked hand in glove with chariot-and-cavalry general Wang Gao; in debate they routinely insisted on precedent alone and would not follow Wangzhi and his allies.
proposals.after: Palace secretariat directors Hong Gong and Shi Xian long controlled the levers of government, were expert in written law, and also worked hand in glove with chariot-and-cavalry general Shi Gao; in debate they routinely insisted on precedent alone and would not follow Wangzhi and his allies.
proposals.reason: Literal also wrongly surnames 高 as Wang instead of Shi.

proposals.before: Zheng Peng of Kuaiji curried favor by memorializing against General Wang Gao's clients for corruption in the provinces and against the Xu and Shi clans.
proposals.after: Zheng Peng of Kuaiji curried favor by memorializing against General Shi Gao's clients for corruption in the provinces and against the Xu and Shi clans.
proposals.reason: 車騎將軍高 is Shi Gao (史高), already named earlier; 'Wang Gao' invents the wrong surname.

proposals.before: Zheng Peng of Kuaiji covertly wished to attach himself to Wangzhi; he submitted a memorial charging that chariot-and-cavalry general Wang Gao had sent agents to pursue illicit profit in the commanderies and kingdoms, and also detailing faults of the Xu and Shi younger kin.
proposals.after: Zheng Peng of Kuaiji covertly wished to attach himself to Wangzhi; he submitted a memorial charging that chariot-and-cavalry general Shi Gao had sent agents to pursue illicit profit in the commanderies and kingdoms, and also detailing faults of the Xu and Shi younger kin.
proposals.reason: Literal also wrongly surnames 高 as Wang instead of Shi.

proposals.before: He earned promotion to Chenliu by crushing the Jiangxia bandit Cheng Zhong; in Yuanshi, when the Bright Hall rose and lords gathered in court, he was called to be grand herald but took ill, missed the rites, went back to his old post, and retired sick.
proposals.after: For pacifying the Jiang bandits Cheng Zhong and others he was raised in rank to governor of Chenliu; in the Yuanshi era, when the Bright Hall and Circular Moat were built and the feudal lords held great court, he was summoned as grand herald; he fell ill, could not attend the guest ceremony, returned to his former post, and was dismissed on grounds of illness.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic invents Jiangxia for 江賊, omits 等 and 辟雍, and softens 病免 to retired sick instead of dismissal for illness.

proposals.before: Otherwise this towering Confucian, broken yet unbowed, might have been the sort of pillar who steadies the altars of state in recent times.
proposals.after: Had it not been so, Wangzhi—grand in bearing, broken but not bent—was a Confucian patriarch who had the capacity to assist governance, a minister for the altars of state in recent times.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic drops 望之, and turns the affirmative 近古社稷臣也 into a hedged might have been.

decisions.reason: 夏侯勝 is the compound surname Xiahou plus Sheng; splitting it as 'Xia housheng' is a naming error, and Xiahou Sheng is the correct English form.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 又從夏侯勝問《論語》、《禮服》

decisions.reason: The same unit's literal also mis-segments 夏侯勝; replacing 'Xia housheng' with Xiahou Sheng restores the correct personal name.
丞相霸 has no surname Bing; earlier 黃霸代為御史大夫 and 霸為丞相 identify this chancellor as Huang Ba, so 'Bing Ba' is a false invention.
車騎將軍高 resumes 史高, earlier made 大司馬車騎將軍; 'Wang Gao' invents the wrong surname and must be Shi Gao.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 亦與車騎將軍高為表裡

decisions.reason: Literal likewise invents surname Wang for 車騎將軍高; the prior appointment of 史高 fixes the name as Shi Gao.
車騎將軍高 again refers to Shi Gao; 'Wang Gao' is the same invented surname and should be corrected.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 車騎將軍高遣客為奸利郡國

decisions.reason: The literal of the same memorial likewise misnames 車騎將軍高 as Wang Gao; Shi Gao is required by the chapter's earlier identification.

decisions.after: For his merit in suppressing Cheng Zhong and the other river bandits, he was raised in rank and appointed governor of Chenliu. In the Yuanshi era, when the Bright Hall and Circular Moat were built and the feudal lords assembled at a grand court, he was summoned as Grand Herald. Illness kept him from presiding over the reception, so he returned to his former post and was later dismissed on grounds of illness.
decisions.reason: The source has river bandits rather than a Jiangxia bandit, includes Cheng Zhong's companions and the Circular Moat, and says illness prevented Xiao You from performing the reception duties. The worker found the omissions, but its proposed English was too literal for the idiomatic field.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 平江賊成重等有功，增秩為陳留太守，元始中，作明堂辟雍，大朝諸侯，征由為大鴻臚，會病，不及賓贊，還歸故官，病免。

decisions.after: Had things turned out otherwise, the imposing Wangzhi—broken but never bent, a master of the Confucian tradition with the ability to aid a ruler—would have ranked among the great ministers of the state in recent antiquity.
decisions.reason: 不然 introduces a counterfactual and the sentence explicitly names Wangzhi. The worker correctly restored those points, but its proposed tense and repeated 'altars' were unnatural in English.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 不然，望之堂堂……近古社稷臣也

claimRevisions.reason: The English name value 'Xia housheng' exists only because the idiomatic mistranslated 夏侯勝; accepting r0001 restores Xiahou Sheng.
